name: Malkiram
title: Son of King Jeconiah
summary: Malkiram was a son of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the royal Davidic lineage during the exile. His significance lies in his place in the Davidic genealogy, which continued the royal line while in captivity.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jeconiah's lineage
keyEvents.description: Malkiram is listed as one of the sons of Jeconiah (Jehoiachin), the imprisoned king of Judah, in the genealogies of Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: The Davidic line in exile
keyEvents.description: Through his father Jeconiah, Malkiram belonged to the royal Davidic lineage that continued during the Babylonian captivity.

keyEvents.title: Jeconiah's imprisonment and release
keyEvents.description: Malkiram's father Jeconiah was taken captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar. Later, Jeconiah was released from prison by the Babylonian king Evil-Merodach.

keyEvents.title: Part of the royal genealogy from David
keyEvents.description: Malkiram is part of the unbroken lineage from King David through Solomon and the subsequent kings of Judah, documented in Chronicles.
